cohort: The study included 68 females with partial X-deletions and 55 with 45,X karyotype (identified from 101,018 individuals who underwent peripheral blood karyotype analysis and were aged >= 15 years as of 2025), along with 130 pregnant women with normal karyotype for comparison.
finding: Females with partial X-chromosome deletions face significant reproductive challenges, particularly infertility, but demonstrate a significantly higher probability of spontaneous conception compared to those with homozygous 45,X karyotype, with their offspring having a high probability of inheriting the maternal abnormal X-chromosome and presenting with varying clinical phenotypes.
mod_finding: Elevated rates of cesarean section were observed in females with partial X-deletions compared to pregnant women with normal karyotypes.
